author: reek
body: `process-exit` was bound twice in the builtin table, ~42 lines apart, and the fold REPLACES -- so the second bind silently won. The winner was a bare `int-ty-default`, the nullary bare-metal syscall, and the loser was `Integer -> [Process] Nothing`, the unary host form that all 53 transpiler plugs emit. `process-exit 0` therefore did not type-check: CDX2001, Integer against Fun.

author: reek
body: Both operations were wanted and they are genuinely different -- free this process slot, against exit the program with a status -- so neither was deleted. They have two names now: `process-exit` is the unary host form, `process-exit-self` the nullary bare-metal one.

author: reek
body: This pins the bind in the CHECKER, where a positive test cannot: a program that uses the name where an Integer is required fails before emit, and fails only if the unary bind is the one in scope. Under the old nullary bind this chapter compiled clean. The positive half lives in `codex/test/process-exit-status` now that the unary form has an x86 emitter.

author: reek
body: It is therefore a discriminator and not a restatement: passing the name to `take-int` is rejected exactly when `process-exit` is a function, and accepted exactly when it is an Integer.
